Name: CIC Modbus Dataset 2023
Summary: Packet captures and timestamped attack logs from a simulated Modbus substation network, covering nine attack types and benign traffic.
Asset / Process: Control systems and networks; Power grids and plants
Description:
The CIC Modbus Dataset 2023 is a set of network captures and attack logs from a simulated electrical substation, published by the Canadian Institute for Cybersecurity. It accompanies a paper by Kwasi Boakye-Boateng, Ali A. Ghorbani and Arash Habibi Lashkari at the 20th International Conference on Privacy, Security and Trust (PST) in 2023.

Docker containers stand in for IEDs and SCADA HMIs: IEDs change voltage values, and HMIs tap-change or switch on overvoltage and undervoltage. Secure devices run a detection agent that reports scores to a central agent. Traffic is captured per IED with tcpdump and for the whole network on the Docker bridge, in PCAP files split into 100 MB chunks.

A benign part holds legitimate Modbus traffic. The attack part covers reconnaissance, query flooding, payload loading, delayed responses, length changes, false data injection, stacked frames, brute-force writes and replay, launched from an external host, a compromised IED or a compromised HMI. CSV logs give each attack's UTC timestamp, target and type. Redistribution is allowed with a citation of the dataset and paper.
